Rather, this was done to them because of their wicked deeds and their earnings. Therefore He said: {You are only being recompensed for what you used to do.}

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 52, verses 21–28:

{21} This is part of the completeness of the bliss of the people of Paradise: that Allah joins them with their offspring who followed them in faith. That is, the offspring are joined to them through the faith that came from their fathers, so the offspring become followers of their parents in faith. A fortiori, when their offspring follow them with faith that comes from themselves, the mentioned ones are joined by Allah to the ranks of their fathers in Paradise, even if the offspring do not reach those ranks. This is a reward for the fathers and an increase in their reward. Despite this, Allah does not diminish anything of the fathers' deeds. Since someone might suppose that the people of the Fire are likewise joined by Allah to their offspring, He informed us that the rulings of the two abodes are not one ruling. The Fire is the abode of justice, and it is part of His justice, exalted is He, that He does not punish anyone except for a sin. For this reason He said: ﴿Every person is held in pledge for what they have earned﴾, that is, held in pawn by their deeds. ﴿No bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾, and the sin of one person is not laid upon another. This objection has the benefit of removing the aforementioned misconception.

{22} And His saying: ﴿And We provided them﴾, that is, We provided the people of Paradise from Our vast bounty and abundant sustenance, ﴿with fruit﴾, such as grapes, pomegranates, apples, and various delicious fruits beyond what sustains them, ﴿and meat of whatever they desire﴾, from everything they ask for and their souls crave, such as the flesh of birds and other meats.

{23} ﴿They pass around therein a cup﴾, that is, cups of pure wine and intoxicating drink circulate among them, and they pass them to one another, and ﴿immortal youths﴾ go around them with goblets and pitchers. ﴿Therein there is no idle talk nor sinful speech﴾, that is, there is no idle talk in Paradise, which is talk without benefit, nor sinful speech, which is talk containing sin and disobedience. When these two are negated, the third matter is established, which is that their speech therein is peace, good, pure, delightful to souls, and gladdening to hearts. They keep the best company and enjoy the finest companionship, and they hear from their Lord only what gladdens their eyes, indicates His pleasure with them, and shows His love for them.

{24} ﴿And there will go around them young boys for them﴾, that is, servants who are youthful, ﴿as if they were pearls well-guarded﴾ because of their beauty and radiance. They attend upon them with service and the fulfilment of their needs. This indicates the abundance of their bliss, its vastness, and the completeness of their comfort.

{25} ﴿And they turn to one another, asking one another﴾, about the affairs of this world and its circumstances.

{26} ﴿They say﴾, in explaining what brought them to the joy and delight they are in: ﴿Indeed, we were before this among our people fearful﴾, that is, in the abode of this world, among our families, we were apprehensive and fearful. So we abandoned sins out of fear of Him, and we reformed our faults for that purpose.

{27} ﴿So Allah bestowed favor upon us﴾ with guidance and success, ﴿and protected us from the punishment of the scorching wind﴾, that is, the punishment of intense, burning heat.

{28} ﴿Indeed, we used to call upon Him before﴾, asking that He protect us from the punishment of the scorching wind and bring us to bliss. This includes both the supplication of worship and the supplication of request. That is, we never ceased to draw near to Him through various kinds of worship and to call upon Him at all times. ﴿Indeed, He is the Most Kind, the Most Merciful﴾. From His kindness toward us and His mercy to us, He granted us His pleasure and Paradise, and He protected us from His wrath and the Fire.

{32} ﴿Do their minds command them to this, or are they a transgressing people?﴾ That is: is this denial of you and these statements they make issued from their intellects and minds? Evil are the intellects and minds whose results and fruits are these. For an intellect that has made the most perfect of creation insane, and has made the most truthful of truth a liar and falsehood, is indeed an intellect from which even the insane should be cleared. Or is it rather their wrongdoing and their transgression that has driven them to this? And this is the reality, for transgression has no limit at which it stops, so one should not be surprised that the transgressor who exceeds all bounds says and does everything that proceeds from him.

{33} ﴿Or do they say: he has fabricated it?﴾; that is, Muhammad has invented the Qur'an and said it on his own accord. ﴿Rather, they do not believe﴾; for if they believed, they would not have said what they said.

{34} ﴿Then let them produce a discourse like it, if they are truthful﴾, [claiming] that he fabricated it. For you are the eloquent Arabs and the eloquent masters of rhetoric. He has challenged you to produce something like it, so that your opposition would be proven true, or else you would acknowledge its truthfulness. Even if you and humans and jinn were gathered together, you would not be able to oppose it or produce its like. Therefore, you are then between two matters: either you believe in it and follow its guidance, or you are obstinate and follow what you know to be falsehood.

{35} ﴿Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators?﴾ This is an argument against them with a matter in which they can have no recourse except to submit to the truth, or else to step outside the requirements of reason and religion. The explanation is that they deny the Oneness of Allah and deny His Messenger, and this entails denying that Allah created them. It is established by reason together with revelation that this cannot exceed one of three possibilities. Either they were ﴿created from nothing﴾, meaning there is no creator who created them, but rather they came into existence without any bringing into being or any originator. This is sheer impossibility. Or ﴿are they the creators?﴾, meaning of themselves. This too is impossible, for it is inconceivable that anyone should bring himself into existence. When these two possibilities are invalidated and their impossibility is made clear, the third possibility is necessarily fixed, which is that Allah is the One who created them. When this is established, it is known that Allah Most High alone is the one worshipped, the One for whom worship is fitting and proper and for no one else.

{36} As for His saying: ﴿Or did they create the heavens and the earth?﴾, this is an interrogation that establishes a negation; that is, they did not create the heavens and the earth, such that they could be partners with Allah. This is a very clear matter. ﴿Rather﴾, the deniers ﴿do not have certainty﴾; that is, they do not have [complete knowledge and] certainty that would obligate them to benefit from the legal and rational proofs.

{37} ﴿Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord, or are they the controllers?﴾ That is: do these deniers possess the treasuries of your Lord's mercy, so that they give to whom they wish and withhold from whom they wish? In other words, on that basis they have restricted Allah from giving prophethood to His servant and Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, as though they were the appointed agents over the treasuries of Allah's mercy. But they are far more lowly and humble than that. They do not have in their hands any benefit or harm for themselves, nor death, nor life, nor resurrection. ﴿Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord? It is We who have distributed among them their livelihood in the life of this world﴾? ﴿Or are they the controllers?﴾; that is, those who dominate the creation and dominion of Allah by force and overpowering? The matter is not so; rather, they are the helpless and the poor.

{38} ﴿Or do they have a ladder on which they listen?﴾; that is, do they have access to the unseen and the ability to listen to it among the Exalted Assembly, so that they report matters no one else knows? ﴿Then let their listener﴾, the one who claims this, ﴿bring a clear authority﴾. How could he, when Allah Most High knows the unseen and the seen, and does not reveal His unseen to anyone except whom He has chosen of the Messengers, to inform him of what He wills of His knowledge? And since Muhammad ﷺ is the best of the Messengers, the most knowledgeable of them, and their leader, and since he is the one who reports what he has reported of the Oneness of Allah, His promise, His threat and other true reports, while the deniers are people of ignorance, misguidance, error and obstinacy, which of the two reporters is more deserving of acceptance of his report? The disbelievers have left no means of scheming within their power unused, but they have done it, and Allah granted victory to His Prophet over them, made His religion manifest, humiliated them and took vengeance upon them.

{43} ﴿Or do they have a god other than Allah?﴾; that is, do they have a god that is called upon, whose benefit is hoped for and whose harm is feared, other than Allah Most High? ﴿Glory be to Allah above what they associate﴾. He has no partner in dominion, nor a partner in Oneness and worship. This is the purpose of the speech for which this passage was brought: the nullification of the worship of anything other than Allah, and the explanation of its corruption through those decisive proofs; and that what the polytheists adhere to is falsehood; and that what ought to be worshipped, prayed to, prostrated to, and sincerely directed in both the supplication of worship and the supplication of request, is Allah, the God worthy of worship, the One of perfect names and attributes, abundant in beautiful descriptions and fine deeds, possessor of majesty, honour and an unassailable might, the One, the Unique, the Single, the Eternal Refuge, the Great, the Praiseworthy, the Glorious.

{29} Allah Most High commands His Messenger ﷺ to remind people, both the Muslims and the disbelievers, so that Allah's proof is established against the wrongdoers, and so that those who are granted success are guided by his reminder. He is not to be concerned with the words of the polytheists who deny the truth, nor with their harm and their statements, by which they turn people away from following him, even though they know that he is the furthest of people from those things. For this reason, Allah negated from him every deficiency with which they accused him, saying: ﴿So, by the grace of your Lord, you are not a soothsayer﴾; that is, by His favour and kindness, ﴿nor a madman﴾, meaning one who lacks reason. Rather, you are the most perfect of people in intellect, the furthest from the devils, the greatest in truthfulness, the most noble, and the most complete.

{30} At other times they say about him that he is ﴿a poet﴾, one who composes poetry, and that what he brought is poetry. But Allah says: ﴿We did not teach him poetry, nor is it suitable for him﴾. They say: ﴿We await for him the vicissitudes of fate﴾; that is, we wait for his death, so that his affair will perish and we will be rid of him.

{31} ﴿Say﴾ to them, in reply to this foolish speech: ﴿Wait, then﴾; that is, wait for my death. ﴿Indeed, I am with you among those who wait﴾, awaiting for you that Allah will afflict you with a punishment from Him, or at our hands.

{32} ﴿Do their minds command them to this, or are they a transgressing people?﴾ That is: is this denial of you and these statements they make issued from their intellects and minds? Evil are the intellects and minds whose results and fruits are these. For an intellect that has made the most perfect of creation insane, and has made the most truthful of truth a liar and falsehood, is indeed an intellect from which even the insane should be cleared. Or is it rather their wrongdoing and their transgression that has driven them to this? And this is the reality, for transgression has no limit at which it stops, so one should not be surprised that the transgressor who exceeds all bounds says and does everything that proceeds from him.

{33} ﴿Or do they say: he has fabricated it?﴾; that is, Muhammad has invented the Qur'an and said it on his own accord. ﴿Rather, they do not believe﴾; for if they believed, they would not have said what they said.

{34} ﴿Then let them produce a discourse like it, if they are truthful﴾, [claiming] that he fabricated it. For you are the eloquent Arabs and the eloquent masters of rhetoric. He has challenged you to produce something like it, so that your opposition would be proven true, or else you would acknowledge its truthfulness. Even if you and humans and jinn were gathered together, you would not be able to oppose it or produce its like. Therefore, you are then between two matters: either you believe in it and follow its guidance, or you are obstinate and follow what you know to be falsehood.

{35} ﴿Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators?﴾ This is an argument against them with a matter in which they can have no recourse except to submit to the truth, or else to step outside the requirements of reason and religion. The explanation is that they deny the Oneness of Allah and deny His Messenger, and this entails denying that Allah created them. It is established by reason together with revelation that this cannot exceed one of three possibilities. Either they were ﴿created from nothing﴾, meaning there is no creator who created them, but rather they came into existence without any bringing into being or any originator. This is sheer impossibility. Or ﴿are they the creators?﴾, meaning of themselves. This too is impossible, for it is inconceivable that anyone should bring himself into existence. When these two possibilities are invalidated and their impossibility is made clear, the third possibility is necessarily fixed, which is that Allah is the One who created them. When this is established, it is known that Allah Most High alone is the one worshipped, the One for whom worship is fitting and proper and for no one else.

{36} As for His saying: ﴿Or did they create the heavens and the earth?﴾, this is an interrogation that establishes a negation; that is, they did not create the heavens and the earth, such that they could be partners with Allah. This is a very clear matter. ﴿Rather﴾, the deniers ﴿do not have certainty﴾; that is, they do not have [complete knowledge and] certainty that would obligate them to benefit from the legal and rational proofs.

{37} ﴿Or do they have the treasuries of your Lord, or are they the controllers?﴾ That is: do these deniers possess the treasuries of your Lord's mercy, so that they give to whom they wish and withhold from whom they wish? In other words, on that basis they have restricted Allah from giving prophethood to His servant and Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, as though they were the appointed agents over the treasuries of Allah's mercy. But they are far more lowly and humble than that. They do not have in their hands any benefit or harm for themselves, nor death, nor life, nor resurrection. ﴿Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord? It is We who have distributed among them their livelihood in the life of this world﴾? ﴿Or are they the controllers?﴾; that is, those who dominate the creation and dominion of Allah by force and overpowering? The matter is not so; rather, they are the helpless and the poor.

{38} ﴿Or do they have a ladder on which they listen?﴾; that is, do they have access to the unseen and the ability to listen to it among the Exalted Assembly, so that they report matters no one else knows? ﴿Then let their listener﴾, the one who claims this, ﴿bring a clear authority﴾. How could he, when Allah Most High knows the unseen and the seen, and does not reveal His unseen to anyone except whom He has chosen of the Messengers, to inform him of what He wills of His knowledge? And since Muhammad ﷺ is the best of the Messengers, the most knowledgeable of them, and their leader, and since he is the one who reports what he has reported of the Oneness of Allah, His promise, His threat and other true reports, while the deniers are people of ignorance, misguidance, error and obstinacy, which of the two reporters is more deserving of acceptance of his report? Especially since the Messenger ﷺ has established, through the proofs and demonstrations for what he reported, that which necessitates that this be the very essence of certainty and the most complete truthfulness. And they have not established any doubt regarding what they claimed, let alone established a proof!

{39} As for His saying: ﴿Or does He have daughters, while you have sons?﴾, as you claim. You combine two dreadful things: attributing offspring to Him, and choosing for Him the lesser of the two kinds. Is there, after this disparagement of the Lord of the worlds, any extent or any limit beyond it?

{40} ﴿Or do you ask them for a reward﴾, O Messenger, for conveying the message, ﴿so that they are burdened with debt?﴾ The matter is not so. Rather, you are the one eager to teach them without any reward at all. Indeed, you spend abundant wealth on them in return for accepting your message and responding to your command and call, and you give to those whose hearts are to be reconciled, so that knowledge and faith may take root in their hearts.

{41} ﴿Or do they have the unseen, so that they write it down?﴾ That is, the unseen matters they knew, so that they would have access to what the Messenger of Allah had no access to, and then oppose and obstinately contend with him on the basis of the knowledge of the unseen they possessed. But it is known that they are an unlettered nation, ignorant and astray, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is the one who possesses greater knowledge than others, and Allah informed him of the knowledge of the unseen in a way that no one else among creation has had access to. All of this is a binding argument against them, by rational and transmitted means, establishing the corruption of their statement and depicting its falsehood in the best, clearest and most secure manner against objection.

{44} The Most High says, explaining that the polytheists who deny the manifest truth have rebelled against the truth and clung stubbornly to falsehood, and that even if every proof were established for the truth, they would not follow it; rather, they would oppose it and act with obstinacy: ﴿And if they should see a fragment of the sky falling down﴾; that is, if there fell upon them from the sky some of the overwhelming signs, a kisf (a fragment), meaning large pieces of punishment, ﴿they would say, "It is a layered cloud."﴾; that is, "This is a cloud piled up, as usual." In other words, they would not care about the signs they had seen, nor would they take heed from them!

{45} For such people there is no remedy but punishment and retribution, and for this reason He says: ﴿So leave them until they meet their Day in which they will be struck senseless﴾; this is the Day of Resurrection, in which there will befall them of punishment what cannot be measured in its extent nor described in its nature.

{46} ﴿The Day when their plotting will avail them nothing at all﴾; that is, not a little nor a lot. Although in this world there may be some plotting by them through which they live for a short time, on the Day of Resurrection their plotting will vanish, their endeavours will come to nothing, and they will not be helped against the punishment of Allah, ﴿nor will they be given help.﴾

{47} When God mentioned the punishment of the wrongdoers in the Hereafter, He informed that they have a punishment before the punishment of the Day of Resurrection. This includes the punishment of this world, by killing, captivity, and expulsion from their homes, and the punishment of the barzakh (the intermediate state) and the grave. {But most of them do not know}; that is: therefore they persisted in what necessitates punishment and severe retribution.

{48–49} When Exalted is He explained the proofs and evidences against the falsehood of the statements of the deniers, He commanded His Messenger ﷺ not to heed them at all, and to be patient with the decree of his Lord, both the decree of destiny (qadar) and the legislated command (shar'), by adhering to it and remaining steadfast upon it. God promised him sufficiency with His words: ﴿Indeed, you are before Our eyes﴾; that is: in Our sight, under Our protection and care for your affair. He also commanded him to seek help in patience through remembrance (dhikr) and worship, so He said: ﴿And exalt your Lord with praise when you arise﴾; [that is]: from the night, which contains the command to perform the night prayer (qiyam al-layl); or when you arise to the five prayers, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿And during the night exalt Him, and at the setting of the stars﴾; that is: the last part of the night, and the dawn prayer (Fajr) is included in it. And God knows best.

The commentary on Surah al-Tur is complete. And praise be to God.
